title: Deconstructing Hello World & The JVM Architecture
summary: Step into the shoes of the Java compiler and virtual machine. Understand every single word of your first Java program.
prerequisites: What is Java & Why Does it Run Everywhere?
learningObjectives: Explain the journey of code: .java source file -> javac compiler -> .class bytecode -> JVM execution
Break down the role of 'public', 'class', 'static', 'void', and 'main' without jargon
Confidently answer interview questions regarding the main method
expectedOutcomes: Ability to write, fix, and explain a complete Java entry point from memory with reasoning

analogy.headline: Why write once, run anywhere?
analogy.story: Imagine writing a recipe in English. If you want an Italian chef, a Japanese chef, and an Indian chef (Windows, macOS, Linux) to cook it identically, you don't rewrite the recipe 3 times. Instead, an international culinary standard translates it into standardized universal culinary instructions (Bytecode). Each kitchen has a certified translator (JVM) that commands the specific kitchen appliances (CPU & OS).
analogy.keyTakeaway: You write .java code once. The 'javac' compiler turns it into universal bytecode (.class). The JVM on Windows, Linux, or Mac executes that bytecode into machine-specific instructions.

activities.title: The JVM Trio: JDK vs JRE vs JVM
activities.content:
To write and run Java, you need three interconnected layers:

1. **JVM (Java Virtual Machine)**: The actual engine that loads, verifies, and executes bytecode. It provides memory management and garbage collection.
2. **JRE (Java Runtime Environment)**: JVM + Core Standard Libraries (like java.lang, java.util). It contains everything needed to RUN an existing program, but no compiler.
3. **JDK (Java Development Kit)**: JRE + Development Tools (like javac compiler, jdb debugger, jar packaging tool). As a software engineer, you install the JDK.

activities.title: Anatomy of the Java Entry Point
activities.description:
Let's dissect each keyword:
- `public`: Accessible to the JVM from anywhere outside the package.
- `class Main`: In Java, all code lives inside a class (a blueprint).
- `static`: Can be invoked WITHOUT creating an object instance of `Main`. Crucial because before the program starts, no objects exist!
- `void`: The method returns no value to the operating system.
- `main`: The standardized identifier the JVM searches for as the execution entry point.
- `String[] args`: Command-line arguments passed as an array of strings.
- `System.out.println()`: Writes text to standard output followed by a newline.

questions.prompt: What does the Java compiler (javac) produce when it compiles Main.java?

hints.hint: Think about the 'Write Once, Run Anywhere' promise.
The file produced has a .class extension.

questions.explanation: javac compiles human-readable source code into platform-independent bytecode (.class). The JVM installed on the target machine then interprets or JIT-compiles this bytecode into native machine instructions.

activities.title: Debugging Practice: Find the Syntax Error

questions.prompt: A student wrote the following program, but it fails to compile with: 'error: cannot find symbol'. Identify the error.
options: String[] args should be String args[]
system should be capitalized as System (Java is case-sensitive)
public static void main must return an integer
Solution class name must always be Main
questions.explanation: Java is strictly case-sensitive. The standard library class name is System with a capital 'S'. system with a lowercase 's' is an unresolved identifier.

interviewQA.question: Why is the main method declared as static?
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: When a program starts, no objects exist yet in memory. Making main static lets Java call it directly using the class name, without needing to create an object first.
keyPoints: Java calls Main.main(args) directly on the class
No object needs to be created before your code begins running
followUpQuestions: Can we overload main()? Yes! You can write other methods named main with different parameters, but Java will always launch with the standard String[] args one.

activities.title: Mastery Verification Checklist
checklist: I can clearly explain the difference between JDK, JRE, and JVM to an interviewer.
I can write a valid Java class and main method from scratch without looking at notes.
I know why Java is case-sensitive and why System has a capital S.
I can explain why main must be static.
